items.what: Zoom the flowchart (Fit brings the graph back)

board.title: The storyboard
bullets: Each card is one scene — the still image it starts from, a few seconds of video, and its narration.
The pill shows where it is: Draft (fast, for deciding) · Rendering · Final · Failed.
Click a card to open its details; drag cards to change the order of the cut.

timeline.title: The timeline
bullets: Your scenes in play order — a wider block runs longer.
The diamonds between blocks set the transition: cut, crossfade, or dip to black.
▶ plays a quick draft preview of the whole cut, scene by scene.
Under the blocks: the voice in each scene and the music across the cut. A gap means nothing has rendered there yet.

inspector.title: Scene details
bullets: Everything about the selected scene — its Image, Motion and Voice.
Apply & regenerate re-renders only this scene with your changes.
Pin keeps the scene exactly as it is; New take tries again with fresh randomness.

canvas.title: The flowchart
bullets: The same project as the storyboard, shown as what it really is — every step of the render and what feeds it.
Drag from a node's right edge onto another node's input dot to rewire it; a filled dot means that input is already taken. Click a filled dot to disconnect it.
Select a node to edit it in Details and to light up its chain — everything that feeds it and everything it feeds; Escape clears that focus.

Ctrl+wheel zooms around the pointer, dragging empty space pans, and Fit brings the whole graph back into view. The zoom is not saved: the layout is derived, so a project opens the same way everywhere.
Add node puts an empty node on the canvas, unwired — wire it up and fill it in from Details. Delete asks first: Add node can put an empty one back, but not its wiring or its render.
